name: Light Hortense Violet
lede: Light Hortense Violet is a bright pink-violet named for hortense, the French word for hydrangea, and classed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955 as a brilliant purple.

sections.title: A hydrangea, not a pigment
sections.body:
Our data files the name under hortense, the flower word, rather than a pigment or a place [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plots it on plate XI at hue 61, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the same area as block 217, "brilliant purple" [1]. In LCH terms it reads as lightness 62, chroma 54, hue 320 degrees: bright, strongly saturated, and leaning pink of true violet [1].

Its nearest neighbors by computed color distance are [[orchid-purple|Orchid Purple]] and [[orchid-purple|Amparo Purple]], each only 2.7 units off, and [[floral-lavender|Lavender Floral]], 3.6 units off [2]. The closest everyday name is [[orchid]], about 5.1 units away [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our 23,781-painting archive has no painting where a close match covers at least one percent of the canvas, as photographed; that describes this archive, not painting as a whole [4]. A near-duplicate by name is [[orchid-purple|Orchid Purple]], the sibling our library lists as the same hue within rounding [2].
